messages.content: You are an experienced sales director. Estimate the probability (between 0 and 1) that this contract will be SIGNED, as opposed to lost or delayed for a long time. Veto holders must all agree for the contract to be signed. Be calibrated.

Deal: Port-Lazen – Kerlis submarine cable · seller: Ondine Subsea · buyer: Nordlink Bay Consortium
Key actors (id | name | role | organization | veto | influence):
- claire_dantec | Claire Dantec | Chair of the consortium | Nordlink Bay Consortium | - | 0.95
- julien_marec | Julien Marec | Chief Technology Officer | Baltis Telecom | - | 0.60
- marion_kervella | Marion Kervella | Marine Permits Officer | Kerlis Coastal Agency | VETO | 0.40
- sophie_lenoir | Sophie Lenoir | Chief Financial Officer | Baltis Telecom | VETO | 0.80
- thomas_riou | Thomas Riou | Relationship Manager | Atlantic Development Bank | VETO | 0.90
- yann_le_goff | Yann Le Goff | Head of Procurement | Kerlis Connect | - | 0.50

Debriefs dictated by the sales rep, oldest first:

[2026-09-15]
Debrief of the kick-off meeting on September 15, Port-Lazen – Kerlis project.

So, first real meeting with everyone around the table. Claire Dantec, the chair of the Nordlink Bay consortium, opened the meeting. She mostly talked about the schedule: she wants the cable in service before the end of 2028, that's her absolute priority. She didn't take a position on suppliers, she stayed very neutral.

Thomas Riou, from the Atlantic Development Bank, was there. He said the bank was "interested in principle" but that a full environmental impact study would be needed before any commitment. He asked us for a note on our experience laying cable in protected areas.

Julien Marec, the CTO of Baltis, asked a lot of questions about the repeaters, he seemed happy with the answers.

Oceanix Cables has also been consulted, Claire said so openly.

Next steps: send the note on protected areas to Thomas Riou by the end of September, and prepare the technical review in early October.


[2026-10-06]
Debrief of the technical review on October 6, with Baltis Telecom and Kerlis Connect.

Very good meeting on the technical side. Julien Marec approved our repeater architecture, he even said he would defend it internally. Yann Le Goff, the head of procurement at Kerlis Connect, was there too. He is harder to read: he mostly talked about late-delivery penalties and guarantees, he wants stronger penalties than what we offer. I don't know if he leans towards us or towards Oceanix.

He mentioned that the award decision will go through a committee where Claire Dantec has the final say, but that the bank must have given its agreement in principle before that.

Nobody has any news of the impact study, I think it hasn't even been launched yet.

Next steps: send a revised proposal on penalties to Yann Le Goff, and chase Thomas Riou about the protected areas note, he hasn't replied.


[2026-10-27]
Debrief of Tuesday's meeting with the Nordlink Bay consortium, Port-Lazen – Kerlis cable project.

Well, a rather positive meeting overall. Julien Marec, the CTO of Baltis Telecom, is clearly on our side: he said our repeater solution was "the most robust technically". On the other hand their CFO, Sophie Lenoir, insisted a lot on the payment schedule, she wants to spread it over four years instead of three, otherwise she won't sign off.

On financing, the Atlantic Development Bank is still waiting for the environmental impact study before committing. Thomas Riou, their relationship manager, wasn't there, we haven't seen him for six weeks now. I think we need to chase him.

The competitor, Oceanix Cables, was mentioned twice, apparently they offered a lower price, but I'm not sure of the amount, maybe ten percent less.

Next steps: send a four-year payment schedule proposal before the 15th, and set up a meeting with the bank before the end of the month.


[2026-10-29]
Debrief of this morning's meeting with the Nordlink Bay consortium, Port-Lazen – Kerlis project.

Honestly, an excellent meeting. Claire Dantec was there, she said in front of everyone that our offer was "the market benchmark" on the technical side. Julien Marec defended our repeaters again, and Yann Le Goff accepted our proposal on penalties, he said it was "a fair compromise".

We presented the four-year phasing, everyone nodded. Sophie Lenoir just said "we'll talk about it after the budget", and we moved on to the next item.

On the bank side, still nothing from Thomas Riou, but Claire thinks it will unblock.

In short, I think we're in a very good position. Next step: send the revised contract within two weeks.


[2026-10-29]
Question: Do you know whether you can secure budget approval if payment is spread as requested?
Answer: The budget is voted in January, and according to Julien, the cable is not in the planned envelope yet.

content: {"probability": 0.15, "rationale": "All three veto holders must agree. Two high-influence vetoes are blocked: Thomas Riou (Bank, 0.90) requires environmental impact study which hasn't launched and has been absent 6 weeks, blocking financing needed before award; Sophie Lenoir (CFO, 0.80) requires 4-year phasing and budget approval, but budget votes in January and cable is not in planned envelope. Third veto Marion Kervella (permits) never appears, also tied to EIS. Chair support cannot override vetoes. Rep optimism in 10-29 debrief is contradicted by 'after the budget' non-commitment and cheaper Oceanix bid, indicating high delay/loss risk."}
